title: SE Enablement - Messaging & Demo Practice
summary: Internal SE enablement session to practice messaging and demo flow. Focus on clear positioning around latency/cost tradeoffs, Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private, and common customer objections. Practiced a 10-minute demo script and refined answers to security questions. Agreed next steps: update cheat sheet, record a demo, circulate security one-pager, schedule follow-up practice session.
next_steps: Marcus to record a 10-min demo video and upload to internal drive by 2026-02-27
Olivia to update the competitive one-pager with new pricing rebuttals by 2026-02-24
Jasmin to add the new demo steps to the playbook and share with sales by 2026-02-25
Ethan to provide updated performance numbers for the 8k/32k seq lengths by 2026-02-23
transcript:
[00:00:00] Olivia Chen: All right folks, thanks for joining

dp

we're at 2pm PST, let's kick off SE enablement / messaging and demo practice.
[00:00:10] Jasmin Ortiz: I'll keep notes. Goal is crisp 10-min demo and 5 top rebuttals. Keep it conversational, not a product dump.
[00:00:22] Marcus Lee: Sounds good. I'll run the demo first pass and you interrupt where you want changes.

[00:00:30] Ethan Park: Quick note

we have updated perf numbers for the new optimizer, share after this call.
[00:00:40] Olivia Chen: Great. Marcus, start us off with your elevator pitch for a buyer who's worried about cost and latency.

[00:00:50] Marcus Lee: Uh yeah so Redwood is, uh, a developer-first inference platform. We make latency predictable and cost efficient by combining a GPU-optimized runtime with smart routing and caching, so you can run the same API across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

[00:01:10] Jasmin Ortiz: Pause

that 'developer-first' bit is good. Try to add a concrete example: 'we cut per-token cost by X for typical chat workloads with prefix caching'.

[00:01:22] Marcus Lee: Got it. So, we often see a 25-40% unit cost reduction with prefix/KV cache and intelligent batching for chat apps

numbers vary by workload.
[00:01:36] Olivia Chen: Great. Now the common competitor push: customer asks why not just use OpenAI's hosted API?

[00:01:45] Marcus Lee: Response: OpenAI is great for ease-of-use; Redwood's edge is control and predictable economics

especially for scale. With Dedicated you get reserved GPU pools and better SLOs, and Private gives you VPC/HSM integrations when compliance matters.

[00:02:05] Jasmin Ortiz: Also mention routing fallbacks

if you hit capacity we can transparently route to a compatible variant to avoid outages.

[00:02:12] Marcus Lee: Yep

automated fallback to compatible model variants. Helps with graceful degradation.

[00:02:20] Olivia Chen: Good. Now demo. Marcus




- 10 minutes, assume a product manager evaluating for a customer-facing chat assistant.

[00:02:30] Marcus Lee: Starting share. Opening with project context, then a quick call to our Redwood API

- create chat completion, streaming enabled

- show response latency in console, then show route config to Dedicated pool.
[00:02:52] Marcus Lee: [typing sounds] Here I'm creating a chat request, enabling streaming hooks. You can see the tokens coming in real time and the per-token cost estimate in the console.

[00:03:12] Olivia Chen: Quick callout

point out token-level breakdown and the trace view for a single request. That's a nice 'oh wow' moment for PMs.

[00:03:25] Marcus Lee: Good call. Also show the rollouts tab

- canary and A/B test to another model.
[00:03:34] Marcus Lee: [imitates demo] "Switch to canary, start rollout 10%"... then show fallback policy to cheaper variant.
[00:03:45] Jasmin Ortiz: We should script the fallback example: e.g., show a high-traffic spike, then show automatic routing to a quantized variant and the request latency staying within SLO.

[00:03:58] Marcus Lee: Right. For rebuttals: if buyer pushes on latency vs quality

we say: pick the model variant for quality needs, then use quantization and the runtime's attention kernels to keep latency low. Also offer a pilot benchmark so we can show real numbers on their workload.

[00:04:20] Olivia Chen: Emphasize the pilot


it's an easy next step to move from interest to POC.

[00:04:30] Marcus Lee: Noted. Now security Qs that come up a lot


can you run through them quickly?

[00:04:36] Ethan Park: Sure. SOC 2 Type II in process, we have SSO/SAML and RBAC in the console, KMS integrations for Private deployments, and audit logs with per-request traces. For Dedicated, data is isolated to your pool and we can sign an addendum for data residency.

[00:04:55] Jasmin Ortiz: Slight correction

we're SOC 2 attestation is Q3 target, but we already have internal controls and customers can request interim compliance docs

don't overclaim.

[00:05:06] Marcus Lee: Good catch

say "SOC 2 roadmap" not "we're SOC2 compliant" unless it's completed.
[00:05:12] Olivia Chen: Excellent. Now let's run a mock buyer push: 'We already have a self-hosted solution via Hugging Face + infra, why switch?'

[00:05:22] Marcus Lee: Response: self-hosting gives control but also adds ops burden. Redwood offers a combined option: Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) for control plus a managed control plane, plus we handle runtime optimizations, auto-scaling and kernel selection so you avoid building operational expertise.

[00:05:46] Jasmin Ortiz: Add cost angle for infra


for 24/7 customer-facing systems, unit economics often favor a managed dedicated pool because of utilization, autoscale, and multi-tenant pooling across teams.

[00:05:58] Marcus Lee: Another common objection: 'We need on-prem air-gapped for PCI/HIPAA'

we can do an on-prem package with customer-managed networking. Note: that requires longer procurement and support engagement.

[00:06:15] Olivia Chen: Keep that as 'enterprise track'. Now demo nitty-gritty: Marcus, when you switch the model in the console, explain quantization choices


- 8-bit vs 4-bit and tradeoffs.
[00:06:26] Marcus Lee: Right. Say: 8-bit gives near-native quality with big cost savings; 4-bit is aggressive but often acceptable for fuzzy tasks; we'll recommend per-workload testing.
[00:06:36] Jasmin Ortiz: Also mention performance knobs: batch window, max latency SLO, and KV/prefix caching. Customers like concrete knobs they can tweak.
[00:06:48] Marcus Lee: I'll weave that into the demo: show the batch config, show the cache hit rate metric after a prefixed request.

[00:07:00] Olivia Chen: Great. Now practice the five-minute rebuttal sprint. I'll play the buyer

"We care about compliance and data retention, will Redwood retain my data?"

[00:07:12] Marcus Lee: Response: By default, Hosted can be configured to not retain prompts beyond request processing; Dedicated and Private give you full control. For strict needs, we offer KMS integrations and can sign contractual data handling terms.
[00:07:28] Olivia Chen: Buyer: "What about egress and latency from APAC?"

[00:07:33] Marcus Lee: Response: We have regions in NA and EU currently, APAC is rolling via partners


iso for strict residency you can deploy Private in-region or use Dedicated capacity in an APAC region if available. We also have smart routing to send traffic to the nearest region.

[00:07:49] Jasmin Ortiz: Flag that "partners" line


be specific: 'partner regions in APAC via our cloud marketplace partners' so it doesn't sound hand-wavy.
[00:07:58] Olivia Chen: Buyer: "How do you compare to Replicate for self-hosted inference?"

[00:08:04] Marcus Lee: Replicate is great for running models; Redwood focuses on production inference at scale, ops and predictable economics, plus features like rollouts, tracing and per-token cost analytics that teams need for productizing LLM features.

[00:08:20] Olivia Chen: Nice. Now demo transitions

after the console tour, show a short benchmark slide with throughput and latency numbers. Ethan, you're on that

what should Marcus say here?

[00:08:30] Ethan Park: Say: 'On our standard 8-GPU Dedicated config, we see p95 latency of ~120-150ms for 8k context in our verified models; numbers improve with batching and quantization.' Use ranges not absolutes.

[00:08:46] Marcus Lee: I'll avoid exact numbers unless Ethan sends the latest spreadsheet

I'll say 'verified profiles available on request'.

[00:08:55] Jasmin Ortiz: Good practice. Also show a real customer use case quickly


anonymized

where Dedicated reduced costs by X and improved tail latency.

[00:09:06] Marcus Lee: I have a short anecdote about a fintech customer who moved to Dedicated for predictable SLAs

-saved 30% per token and achieved sub-200ms p95.
[00:09:18] Olivia Chen: Make that language tight: 'a mid-market fintech saw ~30% unit-cost reduction and met a 200ms p95 SLA after migrating to Dedicated with our batching and cache settings.'
[00:09:30] Marcus Lee: Rehearses: 'Mid-market fintech saw ~30% unit-cost reduction and met a 200ms p95 SLA after moving to Dedicated.'

[00:09:40] Olivia Chen: We're running short on time. Quick feedback on delivery


slow down around security answers and don't read verbatim from slides, use the console to tell a story.

[00:09:52] Jasmin Ortiz: Also avoid the phrase "we're better than X"

 instead say 'for customers who need Y, Redwood offers Z'. It's less confrontational.

[00:10:03] Marcus Lee: Understood. A couple of transcription notes

sometimes the tool mis-labels "KV cache" as "K V cash" in the transcript; but we'll phrase it verbally as 'KV cache' in demos.
[00:10:13] Ethan Park: I'll send the benchmark sheet and an updated cheat sheet for competitive questions after the call.

[00:10:20] Olivia Chen: OK recap and next steps

Marcus record demo, Olivia update the cheat sheet, Jasmin update playbook, Ethan send perf numbers. Anything else?
[00:10:30] Jasmin Ortiz: Schedule follow-up practice in two weeks. Also circulate the recorded demo for feedback.
[00:10:38] Marcus Lee: I'll try to get a cut with captions so it's easy for new hires.
[00:10:45] Olivia Chen: Perfect. Meeting adjourned. Thanks everyone.
[00:10:50] [meeting ended]
